verses.text: Oh, I wish you were like my brother, who nursed at my mother's breasts! Then if I found you outside, I could kiss you, and no one would look down on me.
I would lead you and bring you into my mother's house, she who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the juice of my pomegranates.
His left hand would be under my head, and his right hand would hold me close.
Daughters of Jerusalem, I make you promise: do not stir up or awaken love until the time is right.

Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? She says: Under the apple tree I woke you. There your mother became pregnant with you. There she went into labor and gave birth to you.

Place me like a seal over your heart, like a seal on your arm. For love is as strong as death, and its jealousy is as unyielding as the grave. It burns like blazing fire, like a mighty flame of the LORD.
Many waters cannot put out love, and rivers cannot wash it away. If someone offered all the riches of their house for love, they would be completely laughed at.
We have a little sister, and she is still young. What shall we do for our sister on the day someone asks to marry her?
If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver on her. If she is a door, we will cover her with boards of cedar.
I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So in his eyes I became like one who brings peace.
Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He rented the vineyard out to caretakers. Each one was to bring a thousand pieces of silver for its fruit.
But my own vineyard is mine to give. The thousand pieces of silver are for you, Solomon, and two hundred are for those who care for its fruit.
You who live in the gardens, with friends listening, let me hear your voice!
Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young deer on the mountains of spices!
